answer: Proof of Stake mechanisms prevent Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital, creating a high economic canyon that prevents identity proliferation. An attacker must purchase enough tokens to overwhelm the network, a feat akin to scaling a sable mountain or a vast terrace of validators. Since the cost of acquiring stake grows linearly with the desired influence, an adversary faces prohibitive financial losses, effectively securing the system against low-cost malicious duplication.
